messages:
acme_jane: Hey @support — during our overnight pilot/hackathon we started getting 429s for embeddings, looks like it started around 02:15 UTC. Demo is in 6 hours, any quick options? :sweat_smile:

support_ryan: Sorry you're hitting that. Can you paste the exact error and your account id? Also helpful: are these concurrent requests or a single large batch?

acme_jane: Account ID: acct_89XPL. Error (curl output):
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","message":"concurrent limit reached: 8"}
```
We're doing parallel embedding requests from 10 worker processes, each sending 8 inputs at once.

ops_bender: tagging in — looks like concurrency cap + per-minute token throttle. For embeddings the free tier concurrency is 6 parallel requests per account, paid tiers bump that, and there's also an ingest TPS guard.

acme_jane: Hmm — we thought free tier allowed more for embeddings. Is this a hard block or can we get a short-term increase? The hackathon demo is public.

billing-bot: invoice: acct_89XPL — payment method last used 2025-09-10 returned decline; account placed on soft-limit. Please update billing to remove soft-hold.

support_ryan: Ah — billing soft-limit explains part of it. While the card issue is resolved the system enforces stricter caps. We can do two things: 1) quick mitigation: reduce client concurrency (workers -> 4) and add exponential backoff/retries; 2) escalate for a temporary capacity exception while billing is fixed. For the exception we need approval from Sales and billing confirmation.

acme_jane: We can update card in a minute. Could you hold a temporary uplift until card is updated? We really need at least 16 concurrent embedding slots for 4 hours.

sales_anna: We can approve a short ad-hoc uplift for verified pilots. Need approximate ETA for card update and expected peak qps. If they update payment now and confirm a short commitment (email), we can open a 72-hour uplift. Ping me the billing receipt when completed.

ops_bender: Technical note: if you can't increase concurrency, switch to batching fewer items per request and queue them. Example: instead of 10 workers x 8 items, try 4 workers x 16 items with serialized requests — total throughput similar but fewer concurrent connections. Also enable client-side rate limiter: `sleep` backoff on 429 with jitter.

acme_jane: Updating card now. Will post receipt in 5m. Also trying the smaller-batch approach. Thanks.

support_ryan: Thanks — once we see payment cleared, I'll file an internal uplift ticket with ops + sales. For the ticket we'll need: acct id, desired concurrency, start/end window, and a contact email for post-mortem. If Sales approves, we'll flip a temporary cap to 20 concurrents for the window.

acme_jane: Contact: jane@acme.io. Desired: 16 concurrents for 4 hours starting ~07:00 UTC.

billing-bot: payment: acct_89XPL — card update succeeded, invoice paid at 1714567928.

sales_anna: Got receipt, filing uplift request now. Leaving note: pilot -> potential paid conversion.

support_ryan: Uplift request submitted to ops. Ops estimated response in ~10–15min. Meanwhile keep reduced concurrency in prod to avoid more 429s. :thumbsup:

ops_bender: Done — temporary uplift applied: concurrency cap set to 20 for acct_89XPL from 1714568000 to 1714579200. Monitor for errors and let us know if you still see 429s.

acme_jane: Seeing clean responses now, thank you everyone! Will follow up next week about switching to a paid plan. :rocket:
